# Attribution of Aurelian Basin drying: a review (invented)

This fictional review article exists to give footnote handling a fixture.
Authors, journals, findings and citations below are all invented.

## Abstract

We review eleven invented attribution studies of the southern-terrace
rainfall decline. Nine of the eleven find a detectable anthropogenic
signal.[^1] The remaining two use the older Basin Circulation Model, whose
known dry bias is discussed in section 3.[^2]

## 1. Methods surveyed

Fingerprint methods dominate the surveyed literature, following the
approach of Quenneville and Ash.[^3] Storyline methods appear in the two
most recent studies and reach compatible conclusions.

## 2. Synthesis

Across methods, the central estimate attributes 60–75 % of the observed
decline to anthropogenic forcing. It is *likely* that natural variability
contributed less than a third of the observed change.

## 3. Model caveats

The Basin Circulation Model's dry bias inflates attribution estimates by
roughly a tenth in idealised tests.[^2] Later model generations correct the
bias; conclusions drawn solely from BCM runs are down-weighted here.

[^1]: The eleven studies are indexed in the (fictional) Aurelian Attribution
    Register, entries AAR-001 through AAR-011.
[^2]: Bias documented in the invented technical note TN-88, "Dry bias in
    BCM v2 terrace hindcasts".
[^3]: Quenneville, R. and Ash, T. (invented citation), "Fingerprinting
    regional drying", Journal of Imaginary Climatology, 12, 34–56.
